STOREFRONT PDP ADAPTERS MUST CAP PAGES PER CALL — PARSING IS CPU-BOUND (LC-1537, 2026-09-25, PR #1381/#1385). First real Quince run fetched all 80 PDPs inside the 600 s manual deadline, then parsed every __NEXT_DATA__ blob at once and died 546 "CPU Time exceeded" BEFORE saving ingest_cursor, so every retry restarted at 0. Fix: 20 PDPs per call (QUINCE_MAX_PDPS_PER_CALL, SITEMAP_JSONLD_MAX_PDPS_PER_CALL), cursor saved every call. SILENT-8 FULL DECOMPOSITION (2026-08-26, targeted re-stage evidence): the 8 silent catalog profiles decompose into three distinct classes. (1) SWEEP-STARVATION VICTIMS, healthy when run alone — Annie Selke (73 configs), Edloe Finch (2 configs), Urban Natural (50 configs; its Awin feed DOES contain seating — 137 seating_host_valid — settling the triage's open question); fixed by the 546 sweep fix (budget 90s->40s + per-profile remaining-budget deadline + cron 0,22,44). Neither abort writes any health-log row — the catalog_staging_silence check is what surfaces them. (3) FEEDS GONE — Oroa US, HULALA HOME (both Awin, clean no-feed responses, need dashboard Create-a-Feed), Silk & Snow (Impact 404 catalog does not exist). Lesson: "brand stages nothing" has at least 3 distinct root causes with identical symptoms; a targeted single-brand invocation (catalog-source-management §5) is the discriminating test and costs seconds.

ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED (2026-08-26, follow-up to catalog-ingestion audit): the "Annie Selke pepperjam adapter category bug" does NOT exist — classify.mjs already falls back to _raw.category_program (classify.mjs:131), and a targeted catalog-ingest invocation for Annie Selke succeeded completely (8071 items pulled, 115 seating_host_valid, 73 configs staged, run e86b93b0-23e2-45b9-88e0-0ff2ec84e651, 6.3s). The REAL cause of the silent-brand class: the hourly daily-catalog-ingest sweep STILL dies with 546 WORKER_RESOURCE_LIMIT on most runs (verified in net._http_response: 5 of today's hourly runs 10:00-15:00 UTC all 546) — the LCH-211 expectation that sync_exempt would cure the 546s did NOT hold. Mechanism: claim-first stamps last_ingested_at before processing, so when the worker is resource-killed mid-run, claimed-but-unprocessed profiles stage nothing and stay invisible (no error recorded anywhere), starving roughly the same victim cohort repeatedly (Annie Selke, Zinus, Edloe Finch, Frontgate + the genuinely-feed-gone Oroa US, HULALA HOME, Silk & Snow). Fix directions: reduce sweep memory footprint / smaller batch / free per-profile allocations, tracked under the LCH-224 lineage. The catalog_staging_silence check (PR #920) names the victims; a targeted per-brand re-stage (catalog-source-management §5) un-silences any one brand immediately.

CORRECTION (verified 2026-08-24 against the live embed-knowledge-batch source and cron.job): two 2026-08-10 memories about embed-knowledge-batch were overtaken by the fix that shipped later the same day and must not be acted on at face value.

(1) SUPERSEDED: "throughput is capped by arithmetic not compute; raising limit from 3/run to 5/run carries no 546 risk." FALSE. The live function body records that limit=4 and limit=5 BOTH return 546 WORKER_RESOURCE_LIMIT, while limit=1 and limit=2 return 200. The worker is compute-capped, and RUN_CEILING=2 now clamps the request with Math.min(requested, RUN_CEILING). Acting on the old recommendation would re-break the pipeline. The ceil(limit/2) fixed split the memory complained about was real and is gone, replaced by queue-depth allocation (articles get at most floor(limit/2) and never more than they need; memories take the remainder).

(2) SUPERSEDED: "none of LCH-321's three fix items shipped, the function is still at v14, and the 546s were purely environmental per LCH-223." FALSE on all three counts. embed-knowledge-batch is version 16, deployed 2026-08-10 under LCH-321/LCH-322, and its header documents exactly three shipped changes: RUN_CEILING, queue-depth budget allocation, and a public.cron_runs row per invocation (LC-637). The 546 is reproducible as a function of limit, so it is at least partly a property of the function rather than only of project compute pressure. The reasoning error was concluding "environmental" from "no deploy has happened", when the deploy simply had not happened yet.

CORRECTION — supersedes memory 360bf192-c676-47d6-ad68-9d893511b1c6, which claimed the knowledge-memories embedding pipeline was "silently dead for 63 days." THAT CLAIM WAS WRONG. The pipeline was draining the whole time.

THE MISREADING: I ran SELECT max(created_at) FILTER (WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL) and got 2026-06-08, then read it as "the date embedding stopped." It is not a failure date — embed-knowledge-batch processes OLDEST-FIRST (ORDER BY created_at), so that value is the QUEUE FRONTIER: how far the backlog has been worked, not when it broke. Memories created after 2026-06-08 have no embedding because the queue has not reached them yet. LCH-328 documents this exact trap independently and I walked into it anyway.

THE DISPROOF (the query I should have run first): knowledge_memories.updated_at is bumped by the update_knowledge_memories_updated_at trigger, and writing an embedding IS an UPDATE — so recent embedding activity is directly measurable. SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL AND updated_at > now() - interval '24 hours') returned 180, and 555 over 7 days. A dead pipeline cannot produce 180 writes a day. This matches LCH-328's independent measurement of ~138/day and a counter ticking 790 -> 787.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: (a) the function DOES intermittently return 546 WORKER_RESOURCE_LIMIT — reproduced at limit=4 and limit=5, and a real cron run (pg_net request 11377, 13:17 UTC 2026-08-10) was captured 546-ing; (b) limit=2 and limit=1 return 200 cleanly; (c) enough runs succeed that the backlog drains ~180/day against ~11-20/day inflow, so it self

ROOT CAUSE + FIX (2026-08-10): the knowledge-system embedding pipeline for knowledge_memories was silently dead from 2026-06-08 14:45 to 2026-08-10 — 730 memories (54% of the active corpus) had no embedding, so semantic recall ran on roughly half the knowledge base for 63 days.

CAUSE: batch size, not a poison row. embed-knowledge-batch takes ?limit (default 5) and allocates ceil(limit/2) to memories (Phase 1) with the remainder to articles (Phase 2). The pg_cron job nightly-embed-knowledge (jobid 16) called it with NO limit param, so limit=5 -> 3 memory inferences per invocation. Proven by direct invocation 2026-08-10: limit=5 and limit=4 both return HTTP 546 WORKER_RESOURCE_LIMIT (worker killed, nothing commits); limit=2 and limit=1 return 200 with memories.processed=1, errors=0. A real cron run (pg_net request 11377, 13:17 UTC) was captured returning 546.

WHY IT STARTED 2026-06-08: memory CONTENT got longer. Pre-June memories were short; memories written since are 1,000-2,500-char structured writeups (truncated to 2,000 before inference). Three 2,000-char gte-small inferences per worker exceeds the Edge Function resource budget. The "max 5 safe" comment in the source was tuned when memories were short — a limit that silently rots as data grows.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE (three compounding layers): (1) pg_net is fire-and-forget, so the function's JSON errors[] array is never read by anyone — the diagnostic existed and went to /dev/null; (2) cron.job_run_details showed 245 consecutive "succeeded" because pg_net success means the POST was DISPATCHED, not that the function fini

LCH-321 root cause was misattributed. The embed-knowledge-batch WORKER_RESOURCE_LIMIT (546) failures observed 2026-08-07 stopped by 2026-08-10 with the function still at v14 and its source header reading "2026-06-05 redeploy ... No logic change" — none of the ticket's three fix items shipped. The 546s were environmental (project compute exhaustion, per LCH-223), not a property of the function. Lesson: before filing or closing an Edge Function resource ticket, check whether the project was under a compute event; a function that "fixed itself" without a deploy never had a code bug, and closing it as fixed loses the fact that it is still one compute squeeze from the same failure.

LESSON (verified 2026-07-29T19:20Z, shutdown ritual): a 546 WORKER_RESOURCE_LIMIT response from a Supabase Edge Function does NOT mean the function did not run. The hourly pg_cron job `daily-catalog-ingest` (schedule "0 * * * *") POSTs to the `catalog-ingest` Edge Function; every top-of-hour response retained in net._http_response over 48h came back 546 (6 of 6, 2026-07-29 14:00Z-19:00Z, zero 200s), and pipeline_health_log has been raising cron_http_failure (severity=critical, jira_issue_key NULL) since 2026-07-28T09:15Z. But catalog_source_profiles.last_ingested_at has a most-recent value of 2026-07-29T19:00:29Z — the SAME MINUTE as the 19:00:00Z 546 — with 128/161 profiles ingested in the last 48h. The function is running, doing real work, and being killed on the compute ceiling before it can return. The 546 is the caller's view of a PARTIAL COMPLETION. This is why "the cron is failing" is the wrong diagnosis and "the function exceeds its compute budget and dies mid-sweep" is the right one. Partial completion is the dangerous shape: a run that ingests some profiles and dies cannot report which it missed, so catalog freshness degrades unevenly and silently — same surface as LCH-211. Diagnosis commented on LCH-290 rather than filed as a 7th duplicate of the "[Health] Cron HTTP failures — gateway 401/5xx" class (LCH-269/283/285/286/289/290), which LC-719 already flags for retirement as noise. Health check: `select count(*) filter (where last_ingested_at >= now() - interval '2 hours') from catalog_source_profiles;` should move every hour.

LESSON (2026-07-04, LCH-224): the "Cron HTTP failures" condition EVOLVED under its ticket — the original verify_jwt 401 class (LCH-128) was fixed, but the alert kept firing because three crons (catalog-ingest, pipeline-health-dispatcher, link-attribution-monitor) all fired at :00 each hour: catalog-ingest killed at 546 WORKER_RESOURCE_LIMIT (~62s), the other two 500ing on 5s Supabase timeouts under DB contention. Fix PR #694: staggered schedules (dispatcher :05, attribution :07/:37, catalog-ingest keeps :00) + local 20s timeouts in both functions (fleet-wide _shared TIMEOUT_MS.SUPABASE untouched to avoid fan-out). General lessons: (1) long-lived rolling alert tickets can outlive their original root cause — re-diagnose from live evidence before assuming the ticket description is current; (2) avoid scheduling multiple heavy crons at the same minute; stagger by default. Soak check scheduled 2026-07-08.

articles.summary: Platform-level Supabase traps: pg_net's 5s default timeout means its response never proves an Edge Function failed; redeploying a function missing from config.toml silently resets verify_jwt to true; Edge Functions live only in supabase/functions/; the direct DB host is IPv6-only so CI must use the Management API SQL endpoint; DROP INDEX fails on constraint-backed indexes; and service_role bypasses RLS so RLS alone is not a perimeter. Also: config.toml is the additive in-repo source of truth for per-function verify_jwt, the deploy workflow ignores config.toml-only changes (use workflow_dispatch or touch index.ts), and the shape of a 401 tells you whether the gateway or the function rejected. articles.summary: The complement to observability discipline: alerts that fire reliably and carry no information. Seven shapes — self-latching watchdogs, backlogs posing as invariants, raw counts without rate of change, hard-coded diagnoses that age into misinformation, alerts that cannot fire, conditions that never close, and monitors that silently sample.
